## Recommendation

- **Best bet: South Haven, rated 3 (good).** Fish the boat there.
- **St. Joseph: 2 (average).** The latest report had boats catching fish on spoons, but it didn't rate the bite.
- **Muskegon: 2 (average).** Boats caught fair numbers in 50 to 120 feet of water.
- **Grand Haven: 1 (below average).** This is the lowest of the four on the latest report, though the week before was good.
- **At South Haven:** start around 70 feet of water north of the piers, and be ready to move out toward 100 to 120 feet. Spoons were the lure that worked best.

## Why

- South Haven gets the top rating because the Aug 6 report called boat fishing good there, with the most productive water around 70 feet and spoons catching most fish (South Haven, 2025-08-06).
- Grand Haven gets the lowest rating because its Aug 6 boat report was below average, with fish scattered from the pierheads out to 130 feet (Grand Haven, 2025-08-06).
- I'd expect the warm water (71 to 76 F at the buoys) to keep salmon spread out and deeper than usual, which fits the scattered reports across all four ports (Conditions now).

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (latest report is Aug 6, six days old)
- South Haven, boat, quality 3: "The most productive water appeared to be around 70 feet, with most of the boats fishing north of the piers. … Spoons caught most of the fish." Fish were caught from 45 feet out to well past 120 feet (South Haven, 2025-08-06).
- St. Joseph, boat, not rated: "Spoons were catching most of the Chinook salmon and coho salmon." No depth was given (St. Joseph, 2025-08-06).
- Muskegon, boat, quality 2: "Anglers found fair numbers of salmon in 50 to 120 feet of water. … Green and blue glow spoons worked well along with glow plugs" (Muskegon, 2025-08-06).
- Grand Haven, boat, quality 1: fish "scattered from the pierheads out 130 feet of water"; meat rigs, glow spoons and glow plugs worked (Grand Haven, 2025-08-06).
- The week before (July 30) was better at Grand Haven and Muskegon, both rated 3 for boats in 100 to 160 feet of water (Grand Haven, 2025-07-30; Muskegon, 2025-07-30). That's why I rated them 1 and 2 rather than lower.

**Past seasons** (history, not this year)
- In past Augusts with surface water near 72 F, boat fishing ranged from slow to excellent. The 2024 reports at South Haven and St. Joseph were good on spoons in about 80 to 100 feet (South Haven, 2024-08-07; St. Joseph, 2024-08-07). Other years were slow (St. Joseph, 2023-08-23). So the outcome depends on the week.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before Aug 12, not live data. Buoy surface water was 76 F at St. Joseph, 75 F at South Haven, and 71 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, each up 3 to 10 F over the week.
- Upwelling wind (north to east, 8+ mph) was light in the last three days at all four ports (1 to 2 hours), after heavy upwelling wind the week of Aug 6 at St. Joseph and South Haven (56 and 51 hours).
- Per NY DEC general guidance, Chinook and coho prefer 52 to 58 F, so the surface water is well above their preferred range. Fish are likely to hold in deeper, cooler water.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from Aug 6, six days old. Treat these ratings as an expectation for this week, not a confirmed bite.
- The conditions data was a backtest summary, not live. The tool gave no 3-day wind forecast, so I can't speak to wind safety for this weekend.
- St. Joseph's rating rests on an unrated report with no depth given, so it's the least firm.
- The buoys are offshore; the satellite values near the piers are approximate.
